chunks: And those who disbelieved say: 'We will not believe in this Qur'an, nor in what was before it.' If only you could see when the wrongdoers are standing before their Lord, returning one another's words, saying those who were weak to those who were arrogant: 'If it had not been for you, we would have been believers.'
ai.seo_question: How do the weak and arrogant disbelievers interact on the Day of Judgment according to Surah Saba?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse illustrates the collapse of hierarchical authority on the Day of Resurrection, where the 'mustakbirun' (arrogant leaders) and 'mustad'afun' (subjugated followers) exchange blame, revealing that blind following (taqlid) does not absolve the masses of responsibility. The dynamic highlights how political and spiritual elites manipulate the populace, yet both groups face distinct accountability for their roles in the propagation of disbelief.
